scenario.title: 健身房裡的對話、聊運動習慣
scenario.context: 聊運動習慣一定會講到頻率：常常、有時、幾乎不、一週三次。always / usually / sometimes 放在句子哪裡，是台灣人很少注意、但一放錯就很明顯的地方。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Excuse me, are you using this bench?
lines.zh: 不好意思，你在用這張椅子嗎？

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.en: I've got two more sets. Want to work in?
lines.zh: 我還剩兩組。要一起輪著用嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Sure, thanks. I'll just do my sets between yours.
lines.zh: 好啊，謝謝。我就在你的組間做。

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.en: No problem. You're here pretty often, right?

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I usually come three times a week, but I never come on weekends. It's way too crowded.
lines.zh: 我通常一週來三次，但週末從來不來，人太多了。

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.zh: 聰明。週六根本是動物園。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Do you always train this late?

lines.speaker: Guy
lines.en: Pretty much. I hit the gym right after work, otherwise I just go home and crash.
lines.zh: 差不多。我下班就直接來，不然回家就直接倒下了。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Why are you walking like that?

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Leg day. My trainer went full beast mode on me.
lines.zh: 練腿日。我教練整個火力全開。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Ouch. Do you often get this sore?

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Not usually. But he says no pain, no gain.
lines.zh: 通常不會。但他說不痛就沒有收穫。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Are you trying to get swole or something?
lines.zh: 你是想練成大隻佬之類的嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Ha, no. I just want to be able to carry my groceries up five floors without dying.
lines.zh: 哈，不是。我只是想提著菜爬五層樓不會死掉。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Fair. I hardly ever work out, so I'm in no position to judge.
lines.zh: 合理。我幾乎不運動，沒資格評論。

patterns.en: How many sets do you have left?

patterns.note: work in = 在別人組間休息時插進去用

patterns.en: I work out three times a week.
I'm trying to get in shape.

patterns.note: spot = 在旁邊保護舉重的人

patterns.en: I hardly ever skip a workout.

chinglish.wrong: I go always to the gym after work.
chinglish.right: I always go to the gym after work.
chinglish.why: 頻率副詞放在一般動詞前面。中文「我總是下班去」的語序其實一樣，但很多人會被其他語言干擾放錯。

chinglish.right: I work out every day. / I exercise every day.
chinglish.why: do sport 是英式說法而且偏指球類運動。一般的「運動、健身」美式說 work out / exercise。
肌肉痠痛是 sore。sour 是「酸的味道」，完全不同的字。

chinglish.wrong: Sometimes I am late to the gym usually.
chinglish.right: I'm sometimes late for my gym class.
chinglish.why: 一個句子放一個頻率副詞就好；be 動詞時副詞放在 be 後面。

grammar.title: 頻率副詞的位置
grammar.oneLiner: 頻率副詞放在一般動詞前面、be 動詞後面、助動詞後面。
whenToUse: 常見頻率副詞（由高到低）：always > usually > often > sometimes > rarely / hardly ever > never。
一般動詞前：I usually go after work.
be 動詞後：I'm always tired on Mondays.
助動詞後：I can never remember his name. / I've never tried yoga.
sometimes 和 usually 也可以放句首強調：Sometimes I skip leg day.
具體次數放句尾：three times a week, once a month, every day。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文的「常常、總是」大多放在動詞前面，這點和英文一樣。真正的問題出在 be 動詞：中文「我總是很累」沒有 be 動詞，所以台灣人會說 I always am tired。另外 hardly ever 和 never 本身就是否定，不能再加 don't。

examples.correct: I usually work out in the morning.
examples.incorrect: I work out usually in the morning.

examples.correct: I'm always hungry after the gym.
examples.incorrect: I always am hungry after the gym.

examples.correct: I've never been to a spin class.

examples.incorrect: I don't hardly ever eat breakfast.
examples.note: hardly ever 已經是否定，不要再加 don't。

examples.correct: I go swimming twice a week.

quiz.question: Choose the sentence with the correct word order.
options: I take the MRT usually always.
quiz.explanation: 頻率副詞放一般動詞前。

quiz.question: I can ___ remember where I parked. (從來不)
quiz.explanation: 助動詞 can 後面放 never。

quiz.question: I go to yoga ___ a week. (兩次)
quiz.explanation: twice a week = 一週兩次。

slang.usage: go to the gym 的口語說法。hit 也可以接其他地方：hit the road, hit the beach。

examples.en: I'm going to hit the gym before dinner.
I haven't hit the gym in two weeks. I feel so lazy.
examples.zh: 我兩週沒去健身房了，覺得好懶。

slang.usage: 健身圈用語，形容肌肉練得很大。get swole = 練壯。

risk.note: 年輕人和健身圈才用，帶點玩笑語氣；工作場合不要用。形容別人時可能被理解成揶揄。

examples.en: Dude, you got swole! Have you been lifting?
examples.zh: 兄弟你變好壯！你有在練嗎？

examples.en: I don't want to get swole. I just want to feel healthy.
examples.zh: 我不想練大隻，只想覺得健康。

slang.meaning: 不痛就沒有收穫、一分耕耘一分收穫
slang.usage: 運動界的經典口號，也延伸到工作、讀書：不吃苦就沒有成果。

risk.note: 有點老套，常被拿來開玩笑或反諷。

examples.en: My legs are killing me, but hey, no pain, no gain.
examples.zh: 我的腿痛死了，不過嘛，不痛就沒收穫。

examples.en: Learning a language is hard work. No pain, no gain.
examples.zh: 學語言很辛苦，一分耕耘一分收穫。

slang.usage: 形容全力以赴、狀態超猛，運動、工作、讀書都能用。go (full) beast mode。

risk.note: 帶玩笑的誇飾，同輩間用；正式簡報別用。

examples.en: She went full beast mode and finished the project in two days.
examples.zh: 她火力全開，兩天就把專案做完。

examples.en: Coffee's in. Time for beast mode.
examples.zh: 咖啡喝了，開啟野獸模式。

review.question: I really enjoy ___ in the park.
I got totally hooked ___ that podcast.
review.explanation: 複習第 14 單元：hooked on = 迷上。

review.question: I'm really ___ in joining a running club.
review.explanation: 複習第 13 單元：感興趣用 interested。

review.question: There ___ three gyms within walking distance of my place.
review.explanation: 複習第 11 單元：複數用 There are。

review.question: Can we turn the AC off? It's ___ in here!
review.explanation: 複習第 7 單元：It's freezing = 冷死了。

review.question: My arms are so ___ from yesterday's workout.
